question: I receive the Canada child benefit but have no taxable income this year. Do I still have to file a tax return to keep receiving it?
generated_answer:
Yes, you still need to file a tax return if you received the Canada child benefit (CCB) to ensure you continue receiving it. Even if you had no taxable income, filing your return helps the Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) determine your eligibility for the CCB for the next year. If you don't file, you risk losing future CCB payments.
 
Remember to include all family members and their information, even if they had no income. This ensures the CRA has a complete picture of your household to calculate the CCB accurately. 

If you're not sure how to file or have questions about your specific situation, consider consulting with a tax professional or visiting the CRA's website for more information on filing requirements for CCB recipients. 

Source: CRA – Filing a tax return when you receive the Canada child benefit

- [Canada child benefit and tax filing requirements](https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/benefits/child-family-benefits/child-tax-benefit-overview/benefits-tax-filing-requirements.html)
